Improving access to FV in household and food shopping environments will only make a small contribution to improving population consumption levels, and may only have a limited effect in reducing socioeconomic inequalities in their consumption.

Such disparities are often more closely tied to the social determinants of health, such as education, income, and employment opportunities, rather than just access to healthy food.
